question: By what means does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of the Kaula tradition in addressing the lord of the Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker claims to have become known or to know.
This knowing is attributed to the grace of the one addressed.
The object known is the determination of the Kaula tradition.
inference: By the grace of the lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula tradition.
uncertainties: Ambiguity between jñāta as known and as one who has known
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula tradition.
